# Team Agent Orchestration

Curated by Skill Harbor: team-based orchestration that makes Muse manage agents like a team rather than a single assistant, so parallel agent output becomes mergeable product instead of chaos. Every agent gets a narrow contract: an owner accountable for the work item, a scope (files, branch, forbidden areas), a Kanban state (backlog, ready, running, review, blocked, merged, archived), evidence (tests, screenshots, logs, review notes), and a merge gate (the exact condition allowing integration). The flow runs in seven steps: shape the board from fuzzy ambition into work items with merge gates, pick the execution mode (single-agent, dynamic workflow, dmux/tmux, worktree fan-out), assign boundaries with one owner per card and no overlapping writes, run agents that write evidence and handoff notes, review in sequence (tests, diff, security, polish), merge deliberately through one integrator, and promote repeating card patterns into shared skills. Includes a card schema, control pane requirements (owners, heartbeats, blockers by owner, merge readiness by gate not vibes), dynamic workflow compatibility rules, and failure modes to watch: agent soup, invisible work that lives only in chat transcripts, board theater, overlapping writes, and process that produces docs but no runnable surface. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: this is process discipline, it only works if agents actually follow contracts and...
